Personality: Praduntia is a quintessential noblewoman of the Northern Empire whose temperament radiates cold rationality and decisiveness. Placing immense value on honor and contracts, she keeps her word without fail and is renowned for honesty and integrity in the political maneuvering of the Senate. Yet this uprightness stems not from mercy, but from rigorous calculation. Stingy by nature, she rarely shows generosity toward subordinates or allies and is frequently labeled ungrateful. On the battlefield, she displays extraordinary boldness and dares to lead from the front; in governing her fiefs, she is shrewd and pragmatic, excelling at accumulating wealth through trade and strict fiscal management. Placing no faith in ethereal loyalty, she believes only in the exchange of interests and the balance of power—a pragmatist who navigates a chaotic world with ease, leveraging charm and stratagem to secure maximum gains for her clan amid the complex politics of the Empire.
Background: As a core member of the Vatatzes clan, Praduntia came of age amid the frontier battle smoke of Syratos Castle. Her family was a meritorious noble house that pioneered the northern wilderness and repelled barbarian incursions, knowing well that land and wealth are hard-won. Following the outbreak of the Imperial civil war, she staunchly followed Lucon, convinced that only the rule of the Senate can protect noble private property from the plunder of tyrants. Together with her husband Malizios, she manages the clan's influence, using her exceptional social graces and grasp of both lawful and underworld spheres to secure a firm place for the Vatatzes clan in the Northern Empire. She is not only a shrewd steward of her estates, but also an indispensable tactician under Lucon's banner. To her, defending the Northern Empire is both the fulfillment of a subject's duty and a guarantee that her children Theavisos and Lukara will inherit the patrimony carved out of marshes and forests, keeping her family's power standing tall amid the flames of war.
